domain_restrictions: r is forced to be n minus a minus b, hence r is nonnegative under the stated hypotheses
The variable q is not given an explicit domain; the expressions require a context where powers, finite products, and division make sense
The definition of [n choose t]_q presumes t and n minus t are appropriate integers for the q Pochhammer factors
The definition of (q;q)_m uses nonnegative integers m
The product over i from a + 1 to b is empty exactly when a = b, and then it equals 1
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For every triple of integers n, a, b satisfying 0 <= a <= b and a + b <= n, if r is defined as n minus a minus b, then the quotient of the Gaussian q binomial coefficient of n choose b by the Gaussian q binomial coefficient of n choose a equals the finite product from i = a + 1 to b of (1 minus q to the power r plus i) divided by (1 minus q to the power i), with the convention that an empty product equals 1 and with the q binomial and q Pochhammer symbols defined by the stated finite products.
quantifier_order: For all integers n, a, b with 0 <= a <= b and a + b <= n
Define r as n minus a minus b
For the stated formula, q is an implicit parameter with no explicit domain specified
For each integer t with 0 <= t <= n, define [n choose t]_q by the given q Pochhammer quotient
For each nonnegative integer m, define (q;q)_m by the given finite product, with (q;q)_0 equal to 1
For the product over i from a + 1 to b, multiply the stated factors, using the empty product convention when a = b
For the product over j from 1 to m, multiply the stated factors in the q Pochhammer definition

statement_nl: For integers n, a, b with 0 <= a <= b and a + b <= n, define r := n - a - b. Then the quotient of Gaussian q-binomial coefficients satisfies [n choose b]_q / [n choose a]_q = product_{i=a+1}^{b} ((1 - q^(r+i)) / (1 - q^i)), where [n choose t]_q := (q;q)_n / ((q;q)_t (q;q)_{n-t}), (q;q)_m := product_{j=1}^m (1 - q^j), (q;q)_0 := 1, and an empty product is interpreted as 1.
